whatItIs: NaturesMud Himalayan Pink Salt (known in Nepali households as Sindhe Noon / सिधे नुन) is unrefined crystalline rock salt crushed into fine culinary granules. Unlike heavily bleached industrial table salt treated with chemical anti-caking agents (such as sodium ferrocyanide or aluminum silicate), our Pink Salt is 100% unbleached and naturally tinted pink by trace iron, potassium, calcium, and magnesium minerals.
nepaliKitchenUses: Everyday Dal, Tarkari & Soup Seasoning: Use in place of refined white salt in daily Nepali dal, vegetable tarkari, and curries for a cleaner, rounder mineral taste.
Morning Lemon-Electrolyte Hydration: Dissolve 1/4 teaspoon in a glass of lukewarm lemon water first thing in the morning or after sweating on treks/runs.
Fasting (Vrat / Ekadashi) Meals: Because Sindhe Noon is pure rock salt, it is the traditional salt used for Ekadashi, Teej, and Navratri fasting dishes like roasted Makhana and आलू फ्राई.
Warm Gargle & Steam Rinse: Dissolve 1/2 teaspoon in a cup of warm water for a soothing traditional salt-water throat gargle during seasonal weather changes.
whoItSuits: Suits every Nepali kitchen upgrading from bleached refined salt, fasting (vrat) observers, athletes/trekkers making homemade electrolyte water, and clean-eating households.
monsoonStorage: Salt naturally draws moisture from humid monsoon air. Keep the glass jar lid tightly closed and store away from stove steam; adding a few dry raw rice grains inside a salt shaker also keeps it free-flowing.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Sindhe Noon (Pink Salt) and Bire Noon (Black Salt)?
faqs.a: Sindhe Noon (Pink Salt) has a clean, mild salty taste ideal for everyday cooking and fasting (vrat), while Bire Noon (Black Salt) is kiln-fired with herbs and has a tangy, sulfurous aroma best for fruit salads, nimbu pani, and chutneys.

faqs.q: Does Himalayan Pink Salt contain naturally occurring iodine?
faqs.a: Unrefined Pink Rock Salt contains only trace natural iodine—it is not artificially iodized like commercial packet salt. If your doctor recommends iodized salt for thyroid/pregnancy needs, follow your doctor’s advice.

faqs.q: Can I use this Pink Salt during Ekadashi or Navratri fasting?
faqs.a: Yes, Sindhe Noon (Sendha Namak) is the authentic rock salt traditionally permitted during Hindu fasting days.

faqs.q: Is it fine grain or coarse crystals?
